title: Portfolio pricing experiments for dedicated GPU: burst credits, autoscale options, and SLA rebalancing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Run a set of coordinated pricing and packaging experiments that determine an economic frontier for Dedicated GPU offerings across three balancing axes: reserved capacity (committed GPUs), burst credits (short-term overage), and autoscaling policies (predictable vs elastic throughput). Goal is to produce a recommended portfolio (2–4 SKUs) with mapped SLA tiers and contract/legal questionnaire (SQ) templates for enterprise closes.

Background: Sales and Solutions teams report pushback on existing reserved-only packaging: customers want predictable pricing but also flexible burst capacity for seasonality and mixed workloads. Engineering has new autoscale primitives and quota-based burst tokens that allow a middle ground, but we lack validated pricing that preserves unit economics while lowering friction for buyers. Compliance teams require a templated QnA that ties SKU choices to supported deployment modes (hosted | dedicated | private) and associated security controls.

Objectives:
- Define and A/B test 3 candidate bundles: Minimal Reserve + Burst, Mid Reserve + Autoscale Credits, High Reserve (discounted) with limited burst.
- Run conversational pricing experiments with 20 pilot customers and 60 self-serve signups from website pricing page variants.
- Measure conversion, retention, net revenue retention (NRR) projection, and cost per token under typical enterprise workloads.
- Produce contract language and an SQ mapping that reduces enterprise legal cycles by 25% for Dedicated deals.

Scope: Pricing catalog for Dedicated only (excludes Hosted metered API), integration into sales quote generator, minimal console UX to show burst credit balances, and a security questionnaire appendix per SKU.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive discounts on high reserve increase revenue predictability but lock capacity and may underutilize GPUs (cost risk).
- Burst credits increase adoption but require throttling/guardrails to avoid tail-cost exposure.
- Autoscale-heavy SKUs reduce committed revenue but can raise average unit cost if not paired with sensible cooldown and batching policies.

Deliverables:
- Experiment matrix and ramp plan (pilot -> closed beta -> public pricing page).
- SKU definitions and proposed list prices / effective discount curves.
- Sales playbook snippets and contract addenda.
- SQ appendix (Google Doc) mapping answers per SKU and deployment mode.
- Dashboard queries to track economics (cost per token, avg GPU-util, burst consumption, conversion).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Three SKU candidates defined with price bands and documented assumptions. 2) Pilot with 20 customers started and first 8-week telemetry captured. 3) Contract/SQ appendix drafted and validated by Security and Legal. 4) Pricing page variants live with analytics and attribution tags. 5) Recommendation memo with NPV and sensitivity analysis delivered to GTM execs.
